chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Fats refuses the South, then plays Fort Lauderdale under Florida's segregation law
summary: Fats had avoided the South; at the Fort Lauderdale date a white friend could not sit with them under state law and the white manager could not take tickets inside, so counted the crowd from the bus.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: When you went down south with bands were you playing primarily to black audiences, or white audiences?
Well, that depends. If we went down south, you played to a black audience, or a white audience.
You weren't --
You didn't -- nah, you didn't mix it.
Right.

They did not mix it. And that's another thing, we played Florida with Fats, first time Fats went to Florida they offered him, oh, man, they offered him a mint to come. For he wouldn't take it. Fats had never been south in his life, and all he heard was stories that he didn't want any parts of it. So I said well it's okay, now, with such and such and such and such. He said 'Forget it! I don't need it! Let them keep it!' You know.
He said I'm not going! And finally, anyway, there was talk -- talked him into it, so we got to Miami. Now Miami, Florida, and we had to play outside of Miami, 30 something --
34 miles, Fort Lauderdale.
Right, uh-huh.

So we went there to play, and pulled the bus up there, and Kirkaby was there. Took out the stuff, so Kirkaby sat up the band himself because he was -- he didn't want to pay a valet. He put the few -- valet money in his pocket. He made that himself.
(Laughter.)
And see, I always want to get back to poor Kirkaby, I mean, you know.
(Laughter.)
He's got every nickle he ever stole, and he stole plenty, believe me. He is -- he's doing all right.
You know who he's been owning for the last 40 years, the outfit that -- the singers that -- he owned them then, right before he had Fats. I mean before he came out --
Oh, the --
"Deep River" --
The Delta Rhythm Boys.
Delta Rhythm Boys.
Delta Rhythm Boys.
He still does, uh-huh. And he's had them ever -- anyway.
We were in going to Florida.
They're in Africa. (Unintelligible.)
No, I mean when you were --
In Florida, yeah.
Getting back to the story.

Oh, yeah, yeah. (Laughs.) So we were sitting there, and getting ready to go on and play, and some friend of ours, somebody from New York, came in, Hello! Blah, blah, blah, blah. I say come on back, and so and so, and sit here with us and have a taste. He said all right, all right. I say --
Black friend?
No, no. White.
White, uh-huh.

So I kept petting him down, and he said I mean, after all, don't -- you know where you are. I said come on, man, you're not like that too! He said no, that's the law here. I said what?! State law, he say, no white man can be under the same roof with a black person, none, no where, in Florida. I said I didn't know that. I thought maybe he was -- and he said look, man, I'm white and you're black, I can't come see you --

It wasn't he and -- I -- the thing, you know, I said the hell, oh gee, I'm sorry. I kept pinning him down, now come on with me, because I knew him when we had been stationed together here, in the states, and around places, so
it's almost time to hit. Long, tall policeman come up, and said all right, break it up. Said get out of here. You know, get out of here, he said.

Said well I'm the manager. Said I wouldn't care who you, you're going to get out of here. He said what?! He said look, I'm Fats Waller's manager, and so and so and so and so. Nobody's allowed in here, or can stay when the door's open, they start, so he say well I'm the manager, and I have to take the tickets. He say not in here, you won't.
So in other words, he had to drive -- turn the car, the bus around, and face it to the door, and sit where he could see, and had a stop watch.
(Laughter.)
Stop clock, no kidding --
: To count them, right?

To count them as they went in, and whatnot. That's the way he had to do it. That's the way the night went down, and of course the manager he cannot come in here and collect tickets, money, or nothing. And they didn't let him in.
: How long did you stay in Florida?
One night, two nights, except, you know, because we were moving.
: And out. (Laughs.) That's --
I -- that's the way we did.
